question: Where did Aaron die?
summary: Numbers locates Aaron's death and burial at the top of Mount Hor, with Eleazar dressed in the high-priestly garments at the summit. Deuteronomy 10:6 says Aaron died and was buried at Moserah, after the Israelites traveled there from Beeroth Bene-jaakan. The two traditions name two different places.

reconcile.connective: The leading harmonization identifies Mosera with the desert of Mount Hor itself, so the two place-names mark one death-site, not two.

discrepancy.connective: Steven DiMattei presses the sharpest objection, arguing that Hor and Moserah are two genuinely contradictory death-traditions from rival priestly sources, only later stitched together.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Deuteronomy 10:6
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, reconciling the death-site by identifying Mosera with the desert of Mount Hor (citing Aben Ezra) and by appeal to the back-and-forth marches between the stations.

link.title: Deuteronomy 10:6—Did Aaron die at Moserah, or did he die at the top of Mount Hor?
link.note: live apologetic treatment: argues Moserah is the district, Mount Hor the specific site within it

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Aben Ezra is of opinion, that Beeroth Benejaakan, or the wells of the children of Jaakan, is not the same with Bene Jaakan, nor Mosera the same with Moseroth; but Beeroth is Kadesh, and Mosera is the name of the desert of Mount Hor … it is certain that Aaron died on Mount Hor, Num 20:23, or there died and was buried when in the desert of Mosera …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes the Hor-vs-Moserah geography by identifying Mosera with the desert of Mount Hor, so the same site bears both names. The two clauses are non-adjacent in the note but the ellipsis join preserves Gill's sense (Mosera = desert of Mount Hor, hence Aaron died both 'on Mount Hor' and 'in the desert of Mosera').
excerpts.source_note_text:
And the children of Israel took their journey from Beeroth of the children of Jaakan,.... Not when or soon after they removed from Sinai; for if this place is the same with Benejaakan, as is generally supposed, they had a great many journeys, mansions, and stations before they came to it; see Num 33:31 and besides, since Aaron, according to this account, died at their next station from hence, that was thirty eight years after their departure from Mount Sinai; and it is hard to say what should be the reason of making mention of these two or three journeys here; and whereas they are here said to journey front the place here mentioned
to Mosera; on the contrary in Num 33:31 they are said to depart from Mosera, and pitch in Benejaakan; which is accounted for by their going backwards and forwards, and so both may be true. Aben Ezra is of opinion, that Beeroth Benejaakan, or the wells of the children of Jaakan, is not the same with Bene Jaakan, nor Mosera the same with Moseroth; but Beeroth is Kadesh, and Mosera is the name of the desert of Mount Hor; and it is certain that Moseroth was the twenty seventh station, and Mosera, or the desert of Mount Hor, where Aaron died, was the thirty fourth, and therefore must be distant; see Num 33:30, which seems to agree with what follows:
there Aaron died, and there he was buried; it is certain that Aaron died on Mount Hor, Num 20:23, or there died and was buried when in the desert of Mosera:
and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead; so that though the high priest died, the office continued, and the law of it remained in force, and the tribe of Levi was separated for the service of the sanctuary, as afterwards expressed.
